release_summary.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer dispute tickets and fix whatever causes wrong bills (CL-01), framing the surge as a response-handling gap. Evidence ruled that out: ticket response times were within SLA (E-01) and no tariff change occurred (E-05, E-06), so H-SLOW-RESPONSE was REJECTED. Dispute volume did roughly double from ~600/month to ~1180-1260/month (E-04). Investigation found route completion fell to 0.88 vs a 0.95 target (E-02), but 59% of disputed bills used ACTUAL reads, not ESTIMATED ones (E-03), so staffing/estimate-substitution could not be the dominant cause. Once mdms-export access was provisioned (E-11/CL-04), E-12 showed 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills actually had valid AMI reads delivered on time but rejected at billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, making H-RULE-CHANGE the SUPPORTED dominant root cause rather than field staffing (H-FIELD-STAFFING) or AMI delivery failure (H-AMI-DELIVERY). The defined root problem (PD-1) is that billing import/validation is mishandling legitimate reads since August, driving the dispute surge. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: it ships route-completion diagnosis and bill/read correlation (DA-ROUTE, DA-BILL) plus push_route_update (pending SH-FIELD/K-DISPATCH confirmation), but excludes diagnose_billing_rule_change and diagnose_ami_delivery and any automated bill writes. This is because verification flagged two semantic failures - the released scope targets the route/staffing path, not the SUPPORTED billing-rule root cause, and the route-fix remedy was mislabeled as removing the root cause when it only addresses a minority of disputes - while VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-SPECIFICS remains OPEN and blocks the billing-rule diagnosis before release.
key_points: Root problem (PD-1): since August, billing import/validation is mishandling incoming reads (including legitimate ACTUAL reads), causing wrong bills and a doubling of CRM disputes; slow ticket response and tariff change were ruled out (E-01, E-02, E-03, E-04, E-05).

H-SLOW-RESPONSE (the initial requester framing, CL-01) was REJECTED by E-01, E-02, E-03; H-RULE-CHANGE is SUPPORTED by E-03 and E-12 as the dominant mechanism (billing import rejecting high-consumption reads).

E-12 shows 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills had valid, on-time AMI reads that were REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION at billing import, not missing reads - undercutting both the AMI-delivery and field-staffing hypotheses.

Release decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, shipping diagnose_route_completion_shortfall (DA-ROUTE) and correlate_disputed_bills_with_read_source (DA-BILL), plus push_route_update (DA-ROUTE) subject to K-DISPATCH runtime confirmation by SH-FIELD.

Fixing route completion only touches the ESTIMATED-read minority of disputes (41% per E-03); it does not address the ACTUAL-read majority (59%) causing most disputes.

The field-staffing claim behind SR-R-FIELD-ROUTE-RESOLVE comes from SH-FIELD (E-07), a non-authoritative source with a noted incentive bias toward headcount increase, and is contradicted by E-03, E-10 and E-12.

That same remedy is flagged as 'removes_root_cause:true' but this overstates its impact, since it targets a hypothesis (H-FIELD-STAFFING) that evidence contradicts and would at best fix only a minority of disputes.

output.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer dispute tickets and fix whatever causes wrong bills (CL-01), framing the surge as a response-handling gap. Evidence ruled that out: ticket response times were within SLA (E-01) and no tariff change occurred (E-05, E-06), so H-SLOW-RESPONSE was REJECTED. Dispute volume did roughly double from ~600/month to ~1180-1260/month (E-04). Investigation found route completion fell to 0.88 vs a 0.95 target (E-02), but 59% of disputed bills used ACTUAL reads, not ESTIMATED ones (E-03), so staffing/estimate-substitution could not be the dominant cause. Once mdms-export access was provisioned (E-11/CL-04), E-12 showed 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills actually had valid AMI reads delivered on time but rejected at billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, making H-RULE-CHANGE the SUPPORTED dominant root cause rather than field staffing (H-FIELD-STAFFING) or AMI delivery failure (H-AMI-DELIVERY). The defined root problem (PD-1) is that billing import/validation is mishandling legitimate reads since August, driving the dispute surge. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: it ships route-completion diagnosis and bill/read correlation (DA-ROUTE, DA-BILL) plus push_route_update (pending SH-FIELD/K-DISPATCH confirmation), but excludes diagnose_billing_rule_change and diagnose_ami_delivery and any automated bill writes. This is because verification flagged two semantic failures - the released scope targets the route/staffing path, not the SUPPORTED billing-rule root cause, and the route-fix remedy was mislabeled as removing the root cause when it only addresses a minority of disputes - while VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-SPECIFICS remains OPEN and blocks the billing-rule diagnosis before release.
